title: Unlawful or Unethical Data Collection
description: Homeowner may be sharing personal information (account credentials, device details) without clear understanding of how it will be used, potentially violating data collection ethics or legal requirements.
assumptions: Assumes homeowner may not fully understand data collection practices

title: Inappropriate Information Sharing
description: Homeowner may share more personal information than necessary for account registration and device enrollment, including sensitive device configurations or usage patterns.
assumptions: Assumes homeowner may not be aware of data minimization principles

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Registration data and device enrollment information transmitted from homeowner to home hub may be intercepted by unauthorized third parties during transit.
assumptions: Assumes data may not be encrypted or may be transmitted over unsecured channels

title: Unlawful Data Processing
description: Home Hub may process collected personal data in ways that are not lawful or transparent to the homeowner, potentially violating privacy regulations.
assumptions: Assumes home hub may have unclear or non-compliant data processing policies

title: Unintended Data Disclosure
description: Home Hub may inadvertently disclose homeowner's personal information or device data to unauthorized third parties through data breaches or improper access controls.
assumptions: Assumes home hub may have inadequate security controls

title: Insufficient Notification of Data Use
description: Home Hub may not adequately notify homeowner about how their personal data will be used, stored, or shared after registration and device enrollment.
assumptions: Assumes notification requirements may not be fully met

title: Unauthorized sharing of access code
description: The guest user may share their temporary access code with unauthorized parties (e.g., family members, friends) who could then use it to unlock the front door without proper authorization.
assumptions: Guests may share access codes with others, and the system does not verify the identity of code recipients.

title: Identification of guest through access code
description: The access code could be used to identify the guest to the home hub system, potentially creating a persistent identifier that could be linked to other activities.
assumptions: The system may log or track which guest entered which code, creating an identifier for the guest.

title: Interception of access code in transit
description: The access code could be intercepted during transmission (e.g., via network sniffing, man-in-the-middle attack) before reaching the home hub.
assumptions: The data flow may not be encrypted, or encryption may be compromised.

title: Linkage through meta-data
description: Meta-data about the parties (guest and home hub) could be used to link or identify them across different systems or time periods.
assumptions: Meta-data such as timestamps, IP addresses, or device identifiers may be transmitted with the access code.

title: Disclosure of access code by system
description: The home hub system may disclose the access code or guest information to unauthorized parties (e.g., through logs, analytics, or data breaches).
assumptions: The system may log access codes or share data with third parties without proper authorization.

title: Improper destruction of access code
description: The access code might not be destroyed properly after use, allowing it to be reused by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The system may not have proper mechanisms to invalidate or destroy access codes after use.

title: Unintended use of access code
description: The system might use the code for unintended purposes (e.g., logging, analytics, or tracking) beyond door unlocking.
assumptions: The system may collect and use access code data for purposes other than the intended door unlocking function.

title: Potential lack of lawful basis for data collection
description: Motion/door/sensor events may be collected without a clear legal basis or appropriate consent from users, potentially violating data protection requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub collects data from various sensors without explicit user authorization.

title: Potential over-collection of sensor data
description: The Home Hub may collect more motion/door/sensor data than is strictly necessary for the intended purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the system collects all available sensor data without filtering or limiting collection scope.

title: Potential lack of notification to data subjects
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what motion/door/sensor data is being collected, how it's used, and who it's shared with.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub does not provide clear privacy notices to users about data collection practices.

title: Potential lack of lawful basis for data storage
description: Storing motion/door/sensor events in the Local Event Log may lack a clear legal basis or appropriate retention policy.
assumptions: Assumes the Local Event Log stores data without defined retention periods or legal justification.

title: Potential excessive data retention
description: The Local Event Log may retain motion/door/sensor data longer than necessary, increasing privacy risks and violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the Local Event Log has no defined retention policy or automatically retains all data indefinitely.

title: Potential unintended consequences from data storage
description: Storing motion/door/sensor events could lead to unintended consequences such as profiling, surveillance, or unauthorized access to sensitive behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Assumes the stored data could be accessed by unauthorized parties or used for purposes beyond the original intent.

title: Lawfulness of data collection
description: The Home Hub may collect video data without proper legal basis or explicit consent from users, potentially violating privacy laws and regulations.
assumptions: Assumes the home hub operates in a jurisdiction with privacy laws requiring consent for video surveillance data collection.

title: Excessive data collection
description: The Home Hub may collect more video data than necessary for the stated purpose of recording camera clips, potentially including sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Assumes the home hub records continuous video rather than event-triggered recording.

title: Insufficient notice to users
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what video data is being collected, how it will be used, and who will have access to it.
assumptions: Assumes the home hub has some form of user interface or privacy policy.

title: Metadata exposure during transmission
description: Data in transit may expose metadata about the parties (timestamps, locations, device identifiers) that could be used to link or identify individuals.
assumptions: Assumes standard network transmission protocols that may leak metadata.

title: Unauthorized data disclosure
description: The Cloud Video Storage may disclose video data to third parties without proper authorization or user consent.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud storage provider has access to user data and may share it with partners or advertisers.

title: Inadequate data retention policies
description: The Cloud Video Storage may retain video data longer than necessary or without proper deletion mechanisms, increasing privacy risks.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud storage provider has data retention policies.

title: Unintended data access
description: Stored video data may be accessed by unauthorized parties or in unintended ways, such as by employees or through security breaches.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud storage provider has some level of access control.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Motion Data
description: Home Hub may share motion alert data with unauthorized third parties or without proper consent from the user.
assumptions: Assumes the home hub has access to motion data and may share it beyond intended recipients.

title: Identification of User from Motion Data
description: Motion alert data may contain identifying information that could be used to link the motion event to a specific user.
assumptions: Assumes motion data may include user identifiers or be correlated with user profiles.

title: Location Metadata Exposure
description: Data in transit may contain metadata revealing the location of the home hub and timing of motion events.
assumptions: Assumes data transmission may include location-related metadata.

title: Data Integrity During Transmission
description: Motion alert data in transit may be intercepted, modified, or tampered with by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes data transmission may not be fully encrypted or authenticated.

title: Unintended Disclosure at Destination
description: Mobile App Backend may share motion alert data with third parties or use it for purposes beyond the original intent.
assumptions: Assumes the mobile app backend may have access to motion data and may share it with other services.

title: User Identification at Destination
description: Mobile App Backend may link motion data with user profiles, enabling identification of the user from motion events.
assumptions: Assumes the mobile app backend has access to user profiles and may correlate them with motion data.

title: Location data disclosure through motion notifications
description: The mobile app backend shares motion-detected location data with the homeowner, potentially revealing the homeowner's home location and movement patterns.
assumptions: The motion detection system accurately captures location data and transmits it to the backend.

title: Homeowner identification through notification metadata
description: The notification may contain metadata that can be used to identify the specific homeowner or household, potentially linking the notification to other activities or devices.
assumptions: The notification includes unique identifiers or metadata that can be used to identify the recipient.

title: Location data in transit
description: Motion-detected location data is transmitted over the network, potentially exposing location information to network intermediaries or through metadata analysis.
assumptions: The data flow occurs over a network that may be monitored or intercepted.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: The notification data in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive motion and location information.
assumptions: The data flow is not adequately encrypted or protected during transmission.

title: Unintended data disclosure to homeowner
description: The homeowner may receive motion-detected notifications that reveal more information about their home and activities than they intended to receive or were aware of.
assumptions: The homeowner may not be fully aware of the extent of data being shared through the notification system.

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: The notification system may not comply with applicable privacy regulations regarding the collection, processing, and sharing of location and motion data.
assumptions: The notification system operates without explicit consent or proper privacy safeguards.

title: Lack of lawful basis for data sharing
description: The mobile app backend may share aggregated device-usage analytics without a clear lawful basis, such as explicit user consent or legitimate interest assessment.
assumptions: Assumes the app collects device-usage data from users

title: Insufficient user notification about data sharing
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their device-usage analytics will be shared with external cloud analytics vendors.
assumptions: Assumes standard privacy notification practices may be insufficient

title: Unintended data processing by analytics vendor
description: The cloud analytics vendor may process the aggregated device-usage analytics for purposes beyond the original intent, such as profiling or selling data.
assumptions: Assumes the vendor has broad discretion in data processing

title: Unintended disclosure of analytics data to third parties
description: The cloud analytics vendor may share the received device-usage analytics with third parties without user consent or proper authorization.
assumptions: Assumes vendor may have contractual or operational relationships with third parties

title: Inadequate data retention and destruction practices
description: The cloud analytics vendor may retain device-usage analytics beyond necessary periods or fail to securely destroy data when no longer needed.
assumptions: Assumes vendor follows standard data retention policies

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Video data transmitted from cloud storage to mobile app backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially exposing sensitive content

title: PII in video metadata
description: Video files may contain embedded metadata (timestamps, device identifiers, account info) that can identify the homeowner

title: Location tracking via video metadata
description: Video files may contain GPS coordinates or location information that tracks the homeowner's movements and activities

title: Inappropriate data processing
description: Mobile app backend may process video data in ways that could affect the homeowner's dignity (e.g., storing beyond necessary time, sharing with third parties without consent)

title: Unintended data usage
description: Video data retrieved for playback may be used for purposes other than intended (e.g., analytics, training, sharing with advertisers)
